title: Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
key_facts: Apple's App Store rules now more explicitly ban 'nudify' apps that use AI to generate intimate images of people without their consent.
The changes were announced on Friday 16 Oct 2026.
Developers 'must proactively prevent and remove' nonconsensual sexual images as part of Apple's content moderation requirements.
Developers who 'fail to implement adequate safeguards' or 'don't remedy violations after notice' may be removed from the App Store.
Apple also clarified a rule against 'bait-and-switch' apps that add or change features, including 'nudification', after approval.
Apps that facilitate human trafficking or the exploitation of children will be pulled and 'blocked from alternative distribution'.

The changes follow criticism of Apple after X users used Grok earlier this year to make nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes, including of minors; Apple did not pull X or Grok but told senators it threatened to.
In July a San Francisco city attorney ordered Apple to remove 13 'nudify' apps, which Apple said it did.
